subject.title: [Bug]: embedded prompt cache breaks across room-event, policy, and Responses boundaries

question: Should OpenClaw accept the linked PR’s contract that keeps protected tool schemas prompt-stable while an immutable current-turn policy controls executable authority before hooks and side effects?
rationale: Tests, sanitized telemetry, current-main gaps, and the Codex contract support the architecture, but visibility-versus-authority semantics for protected core and plugin tools are a security boundary that automation should not approve alone.

options.title: Approve stable visibility
options.body: Accept the immutable pre-execution policy contract and proceed with final exact-head review and landing of the linked PR.

options.title: Revise the boundary
options.body: Require narrower trusted-internal grants, different protected-tool visibility, or a different policy persistence contract before landing.

recommendation.title: Approve stable visibility
recommendation.body: Accept the immutable pre-execution policy contract and proceed with final exact-head review and landing of the linked PR.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history shows the strongest ownership across embedded stream resolution, OpenAI provider routing, and central tool construction.
